DCRU pays ONE tranche a year rather than clean calendar halves: the audited Distribution Statement (p.151, FY end 31 Dec 2024) discloses a single undivided cash distribution of 3.58 US cents ($42,590k) 'for the period from 1 July 2023 to 30 June 2024' -- a period that straddles FY2023 (H2) and FY2024 (H1) in roughly equal, but UNDISCLOSED, proportions. No split of that $ amount or rate between the two halves is given anywhere in the AR, so per the spec we do not invent one; the whole tranche is tagged cash_paid since it was the amount actually paid to Unitholders during FY2024 and its period begins in the prior FY. Separately, a 2H2024 distribution (1.80 US cents, period 1/7/2024-31/12/2024) was declared as a Subsequent Event (announced 12 Feb 2025) -- unambiguously in respect of FY2024, tagged accrual. The audited 'Distribution per Unit' headline row (3.60c) is computed as Amount available for distribution / units (a distributable-income-per-unit metric), NOT as a sum of calendar-year-matched declared tranches -- it does not literally equal either the printed cash tranche rate (3.58c) or a clean calendar sum. Because the FY2024-in-respect-of portion of the straddling tranche is not separately disclosed, accrual_sum (1.80, the only unambiguous FY2024 accrual tranche) does not reach headline_dpu (3.60). This is an honest, expected mismatch given DCRU's rolling record-date distribution mechanic -- not an extraction error.

Same DCRU straddling mechanic as FY2024 (see that record's note). The audited Distribution Statement (p.156, FY end 31 Dec 2025) discloses one undivided cash distribution of 3.60 US cents ($46,779k, includes a ~$31k reversal from FY2024 buybacks per footnote 4) 'for the period from 1 July 2024 to 30 June 2025' -- straddling FY2024 (H2) and FY2025 (H1) in undisclosed proportions; tagged cash_paid (paid during FY2025, period begins in prior FY). The IR highlights slide (p.29, NOT the audited statement) separately claims 'Full-Year 2025 Distribution' = 1H25 (1.80c) + 2H25 (1.80c) = 3.60c, but 2H25 was only announced as a Subsequent Event on 4 Feb 2026 (to be paid by 31 Mar 2026) and is not yet part of the audited cash statement -- so this highlight total is an accrual-basis reconstruction, not what was actually paid in FY2025. We use only the audited Distribution Statement + Subsequent Events note per the spec, giving accrual_sum=1.80 (2H2025 tranche only) vs headline_dpu=3.60 (a distributable-income/units ratio, not a tranche sum). Honest mismatch, consistent with FY2024's record; not invented/forced to balance.
